images.title: HCF × LCM = Product
images.purpose: Show the product 105 × 95 as a row of prime tiles that splits into the LCM and one leftover 5, which is the HCF.
images.composition: One row of five prime tiles in the centre, four teal tiles under one brace and a fifth purple tile set slightly apart at the right end, with one line above and one below, and wide margins.
exact_structure: Below it, one row of exactly 5 square tiles, left to right: 3, 5, 7, 19 in teal #0072B2, then a small gap, then a fifth tile 5 in reddish purple #CC79A7.
A teal brace above only the first four teal tiles (3, 5, 7, 19) with the label LCM = 1995.
A reddish purple ring around the purple 5 tile with the label HCF = 5 beneath it.
rejection: more or fewer than 5 tiles, or tiles other than 3, 5, 5, 7, 19
an LCM other than 1995, an HCF other than 5, or a product other than 9975
the brace covering the purple 5 tile
any of the numbers 45, 275, 352, 222 or 370 appearing
images.takeaway: The product of two numbers is the LCM times the HCF.
images.description: The prime tiles 3, 5, 7, 19 and 5 of 105 × 95 = 9975, with the first four braced as LCM 1995 and the last 5 ringed as HCF 5.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on discovering HCF × LCM = product.
images.teaching_notes: Count the tiles: all five make the product, four make the LCM, and the one left over is the HCF.

image_decisions.why: Splitting one row of prime tiles makes the rule visible instead of just a calculation.
